title: Heun's Method: Predict, Then Correct
topic: Heun's method (improved Euler, explicit trapezoidal rule, Runge-Kutta of order 2). Plain Euler reads the slope only at the start of a step and drifts on a curving solution. Heun first predicts the endpoint with an ordinary Euler step, then evaluates the slope there and averages the two slopes to take the real step: k1 = f(t_n, y_n), k2 = f(t_n + h, y_n + h k1), y_{n+1} = y_n + (h/2)(k1 + k2). One extra slope evaluation lifts the order from one to two.

beats.narration: Euler takes one slope per step, and on a curving solution it drifts. What if we looked ahead before committing to a step?

elements.content: Hook: look ahead before you step.

beats.narration: Here Euler reads the slope only at the start of each step. Because the true curve keeps bending away, every step lands a little short, and the gap grows.

elements.content: True solution y = e^t in violet
Euler polyline in rose, three steps, drifting below the true curve
Euler uses the start-of-step slope only.

beats.narration: Heun's idea has two stages. First, predict the endpoint with an ordinary Euler step. Then read the slope at that predicted point, average it with the starting slope, and take the real step with that average.

elements.content: Predictor: Euler tangent from the start point reaching a ghost point at the interval end
Slope sample at the predicted point
Averaged-slope chord landing the corrected point near the true curve

beats.narration: Write it down. k one is the slope at the start, k two the slope at the predicted point, and the step adds h times their average. One extra evaluation, and the accuracy jumps to order two, a Runge Kutta method of order two.

elements.content: k₂ = f(tₙ + h, yₙ + h k₁)

beats.narration: Now march the whole interval with that averaged slope. Heun's points hug the true curve while plain Euler keeps falling behind, at the very same step size.

elements.content: True curve in violet with Heun's points marching along it (teal) and Euler drifting below (rose)
Live readout of the error of each method at the current step

beats.narration: Predict with one slope, correct with the average of two. A little more work each step, a much closer fit.

elements.content: One average of two slopes — order two.
Heun = improved Euler = explicit trapezoidal rule.
